Despite it not seeming like that, these kind of studies are actually more expensive than you'd believe.

Most of the issue comes from developing a methodology, which requires quite a lot of time and effort from Psychologists/Sociologists. Given that the foundations of Psychology/Sociology are much worse than the nearest thing that is actually a science (Neurochemistry), this is actually quite hard. So, there's a lot of man-hours that get eaten up navigating around the fact that the field is fundamentally a complete mess.

Next, there's the issues of tracking down lesbians who are willing to deal with Psychologists. Nobody wants some asshole digging around their life for what appears to be no reason, so usually Psychologists have to throw money at people in order to collect data. This inherently causes some degree of bias, so the Psychologist actually has to figure out how to reduce this.

Last, there's the fact that these people have to try to get this shitty result published, and that's even harder given the fact that publishers are corrupt. I'd imagine that this is worse in fields that aren't quite science, although it's sort of bad in actual scientific fields.

Combined with the further issue that there's probably tons of other problems I'm not quite qualified to point out, and you get the sad result that Psychology is actually about as expensive as it seems. This isn't something that can be navigated around very easily either; Psychologists aren't known for handling money well, but sending someone to forcibly cut the costs is a great way to butcher the study; you'd get results even Psychologists wouldn't accept!

(I'm not claiming that there's no corruption here, but the corruption is probably not as bad as you think.)
